acceptanceCriteria: Spec amendment in docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md: numbered proposed requirements for pool acquire/release on a live attempt (fencing by attempt+generation, waiting/queueing like a pooled claim, independence and exclusion rules applied at acquire time, release quarantines the exact allocation, lease/heartbeat/run/gate use the current allocation, replay returns the original receipt-bound allocation), failure modes and rollback.

CLI `corvint-tasks pool acquire --attempt ID --generation G --pool ID --request-id ID` and `pool release --attempt ID --generation G --allocation SHA --request-id ID` implemented through the transactional writer, with focused tests per requirement including stale-generation refusal, double acquire, release of a foreign allocation, and an attempt that completes while holding an acquired member.
Existing `claim --pool` behaviour unchanged (regression tests pass); GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#696 answered and closed after merge.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#696 (2026-10-08). A pool member can only be allocated by `claim --pool`; an attempt cannot acquire a member later or return it early. Adopter measurement on a 4-member pool: after authors claimed with --pool, about 70% of 688 held member-minutes were idle (vs ~21% when a runner claimed lanes only for commands), and sessions saw no free lane while members sat idle. The workaround (release HANDOFF then reclaim with --pool) costs two queue writes, a new generation and session context, plus a quarantine sweep (median 2.5 min) per cycle. Request: just-in-time `pool acquire` / `pool release` on a live attempt, with lease, heartbeat, run and fencing using whatever allocation the attempt currently holds and #480/#586 independence/exclusion rules applied at acquire time.

completion.reason: Delivered in beamfall/corvint#699 (merge 2d74f67d); focused tests, doc gates, dogfood bind/check/seal and independent review passed; evidence is the sha256 of the lane and batch build-logs at the merge commit.

title: corvint-tasks pool: a live attempt can acquire and release a pool member (just-in-time lane use, #696)
